newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alfa Q2 growth linked to rising volumes.
newsitem.headline: Alfa Q2 growth linked to rising volumes.

text.p: Mexican conglomerate Alfa SA racked up impressive growth in revenues and cash flow in the second quarter, as rising volumes offset price weakness in some products, analysts said on Thursday.

The company, whose products range from yoghurt and cold meats to telephone services, steel and petrochemicals, is likely to keep posting strong financial results as more production capacity comes on line, they said.

"The theme of the quarter is that we have large volume increases offsetting modest price declines," said Robert Fleming & Co. coporate analyst Terry Sigler. "That is the theme that will repeat itself for the next few quarters."
The company has a high percentage of dollar-denominated revenues, but its peso earnings also rose.

"They were a lot better than expected. They showed very strong quarter-on-quarter growth in EBITDA," said Goldman Sachs corporate analyst Kerry McHugh, referring to earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization -- a measure of cash flow.
"Every division came in higher than expected," she added. "The report bodes very well for the rest of the year."
Alfa showed a 13 percent increase in cash from operations in the second quarter to $222 million, it said in a statement.
"This has allowed Alfa to continue its aggressive investment plans, while maintaining a healthy financial condition," the company said.
"They have a lot of capacity coming on line, and they were able to achieve volume growth that overcame some slight price weaknesses," said Paribas conglomerate analyst Alexander Ryshawy.

"What Alfa has been doing is investing heavily since the beginning of this year in increasing their production capacity, principally in steel and petrochemicals, in order to have volume growth," Ryshawy said. "That has helped them even though there has been some slight weakness in their commodity prices, such as petrochemicals and steel."
The company said operations in the quarter "were very satisfactory," as it reached new levels of production and sales volume.
"Average prices in dollars increased slightly, although in real peso terms they maintained a similar level to that reported in the first quarter."
Revenues increased 10 percent in dollar terms compared with the first quarter of the year.

Operating income increased 17 percent as the cost of some raw materials dropped, a higher revenue base allowed for better absorption of fixed costs and the unit cost of certain items, such as natural gas, was reduced, it added.
